To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

extreme non-cooperation, fear and an excessive amount of treatment were the main indications for the use of general anaesthesia for dental treatment in the Helsinki PHS and that the indications for the use and the treatments provided were influenced by personal and medical characteristics and the immigration background.
DGA was mainly used for patients with extreme non-cooperation, fear and an excessive treatment need, and the treatments provided under DGA were mostly restorative and surgical.
